Hwei.escape: Hwei has no mobility, so right after Hwei E Subject: Torment is down, your ally has a chance to close the distance. Follow from behind and place Soraka E Equinox along Hwei’s path.
Hwei.combo: After landing Soraka Q Starcall on Hwei, heal an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. When you have a chance to catch Hwei, apply Soraka Q Starcall’s slow first, then layer Soraka E Equinox. Don’t place Soraka E Equinox first and expect it to root him on its own.
Hwei.build: In the early game, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads. Most of Hwei’s damage is magic, and Soraka has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Hwei.fight: Instead of stepping forward to look for a kill, land Soraka Q Starcall to restore health and heal an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. Right after Hwei E Subject: Torment is used to poke or clear the wave, your ally has a chance to close the distance. Place Soraka E Equinox where Hwei will pass to help them engage.
Hwei.laning: If Hwei’s first spell hits, don’t stay in place; move to break his combo. Soraka Q Starcall takes longer to land from far away, so aim for where Hwei will be when he retreats. If Soraka Q Starcall keeps missing, ease off the poke and conserve mana.
Hwei.teamfight: Heal from the very back of your team, preferably outside the enemy’s vision. Take a wide route around zones Hwei has placed or passages blocked by his eye, and if an ally is caught by Hwei E Subject: Torment, reposition to avoid his follow-up spells. Soraka R Wish heals allies regardless of distance, so keep an eye on fights in other lanes.
Hwei.watch: If Hwei E Subject: Torment roots or pulls you in, follow-up damage can quickly land. If the first spell hits, move immediately to avoid the second spell and the Hwei P Signature of the Visionary explosion. Hwei Q Subject: Disaster deals damage based on your max health, so move out of its indicated area.

Heimerdinger.phase: A head-on trade in front of the turret favors Heimerdinger in the early game, so build magic resistance and hold on with Soraka Q Starcall. In the mid and late game, Soraka R Wish has a shorter cooldown and can affect fights in other lanes. In late-game teamfights, keep Heimerdinger R UPGRADE!!! in mind: don’t group in one spot, and heal from behind your team.
Heimerdinger.build: In the early game, hold on with Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury’s Treads. Heimerdinger’s main damage is magic, so build magic resistance first.
Heimerdinger.combo: Land Soraka Q Starcall on Heimerdinger first, then heal an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. When Soraka Q Starcall slows him, layer Soraka E Equinox to aim for a root. If you need to land Soraka Q Starcall quickly, cast it at close range.
Heimerdinger.escape: Heimerdinger has no mobility, so if you manage to approach him, place Soraka E Equinox to help your team engage.
Heimerdinger.fight: Don’t trade head-on in front of the turret; poke with Soraka Q Starcall to restore health. If the distance closes, place Soraka E Equinox along Heimerdinger’s path.
Heimerdinger.laning: Keep landing Soraka Q Starcall and transfer the resulting healing to an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. If Soraka Q Starcall keeps missing, stop poking and conserve mana. When it’s too dangerous to check brush yourself, use Soraka Q Starcall to check vision and save Soraka E Equinox for fights.
Heimerdinger.teamfight: Heal from the very back of your team, preferably outside the enemy’s vision. When Heimerdinger R UPGRADE!!! is ready, don’t group with allies in a narrow passage or at one spot in front of an objective. If an ally has lost enough health for Soraka P Salvation’s speed boost to appear, help heal them with Soraka R Wish, but protect your own position first.
Heimerdinger.watch: When you see the landing indicator, move sideways to avoid the center; if it hits you, get out of turret range.

Braum.build: In the early game, withstand Braum’s magic damage with Null-Magic Mantle. Braum’s stun and knock-up are especially dangerous for Soraka, who has no mobility, so choose Mercury’s Treads.
Braum.combo: When Braum E Unbreakable’s shield is down or you can hit from the side, land Soraka Q Starcall first, then heal an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. If Braum engages, apply Soraka Q Starcall’s slow first and layer Soraka E Equinox to aim for a root.
Braum.escape: Right after Braum W Stand Behind Me is down, look for a chance to close in and land Soraka E Equinox. If Braum P Concussive Blows marks you, don’t engage; move out of range before the stacks fill.
Braum.fight: Keep your distance so Braum Q Winter’s Bite and his basic attacks can’t reach you, and land Soraka Q Starcall to restore health. Right after Braum W Stand Behind Me is down, look for a chance to block his movement by placing Soraka E Equinox along his engage route. If Braum E Unbreakable is active, don’t keep attacking from the front.
Braum.laning: Stand behind minions to reduce Braum Q Winter’s Bite’s chances of starting a mark. Save Soraka E Equinox for when Braum engages instead of using it to poke. If Soraka Q Starcall keeps missing, stop forcing the poke and conserve mana.
Braum.phase: In the mid and late game, Soraka R Wish has a shorter cooldown and can affect fights in other lanes. The available information isn’t enough to say which champion is stronger in the mid and late game.
Braum.teamfight: Maintain healing range from the very back of your team, preferably outside the enemy’s vision. Avoid the straight path and slow zone from Braum R Glacial Fissure, and look for an angle where your allies can attack around the front blocked by Braum E Unbreakable. Use Soraka R Wish on an ally who has lost a lot of health to increase the healing.
Braum.watch: Avoid Braum Q Winter’s Bite by standing behind minions, and if Braum P Concussive Blows marks you, move out of range before you’re stunned. Watch Braum R Glacial Fissure’s cast animation and move sideways out of its straight path; also avoid the slow zone it leaves behind. While Braum E Unbreakable blocks projectiles from the front, wait for the shield to lower or line up an angle from the side.

Alistar.fight: Once Alistar Q Pulverize and Alistar W Headbutt are down, reposition and poke with Soraka Q Starcall. After landing Soraka Q Starcall and healing, restore an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. If Alistar R Unbreakable Will is active, back off and wait out its duration.
Alistar.teamfight: Heal from the very back of your team, preferably outside the enemy’s vision, and protect your own position first. If Alistar R Unbreakable Will is active, back off; if you can’t retreat, place Soraka E Equinox after he activates R to stop his engage. Use Soraka R Wish when you can save an ally who has lost a lot of health.
Alistar.laning: When Alistar can engage, save Soraka E Equinox to stop him instead of using it to poke. When casting Soraka Q Starcall from range, aim for where the opponent will be after last-hitting and stepping back. If it keeps missing, ease off the poke to conserve mana.
Alistar.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first to withstand Alistar’s magic damage in the early game. Choose Mercury’s Treads, and prioritize magic resistance over armor afterward.
Alistar.combo: Apply a slow with Soraka Q Starcall, then layer Soraka E Equinox to aim for a root as the zone expires. If Soraka Q Starcall hits an enemy champion and grants Rejuvenation, heal an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion.
Alistar.escape: Right after Alistar W Headbutt and Alistar Q Pulverize are down, look for a chance to step up and poke or reposition. In particular, when Alistar W Headbutt is down, place Soraka E Equinox along his path to stop his engage.
Alistar.phase: In the early game, keep your distance and stay safe from Alistar’s engage, since Soraka has no mobility. In the mid and late game, Soraka R Wish has a shorter cooldown, so watch fights in other lanes and make an impact with your healing.
Alistar.watch: If Alistar W Headbutt closes the distance, Alistar Q Pulverize can knock you up, followed by Alistar E Trample’s stun, so keep your distance. Near a turret, don’t give Alistar room to circle around and use Alistar Q Pulverize and Alistar W Headbutt to push Soraka under it.

Bard.watch: Bard Q Cosmic Binding stuns if it hits a wall or a second target, so don’t stand with your back to a wall or in a line with an ally or minion. Bard E Magical Journey can bring him in from the flank, so don’t leave that approach open. Don’t commit your attacks before Bard R Tempered Fate’s damage immunity ends.
Bard.build: In the early game, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads. Most of Bard’s damage is magic, so build magic resistance, but prioritize tenacity when a Bard Q Cosmic Binding stun could lead to focused attacks.
Bard.combo: After landing Soraka Q Starcall on Bard, heal an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. To aim for a root, apply Soraka Q Starcall’s slow first, then layer Soraka E Equinox. Right after Bard uses Bard E Magical Journey, place Soraka E Equinox along his escape route.
Bard.escape: Right after Bard E Magical Journey is down, look for a chance to close the distance. Find a position where you can avoid Bard Q Cosmic Binding’s stun, then layer Soraka E Equinox after Soraka Q Starcall’s slow to catch him.
Bard.fight: Trade by landing Soraka Q Starcall on Bard to heal, then transferring that health to an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. When Bard can come in with Bard E Magical Journey, save Soraka E Equinox along his engage route instead of using it to poke. Look for a chance to close the distance after Bard E Magical Journey is down.
Bard.laning: If Bard W Caretaker’s Shrine appears in lane, walk over it to trigger and remove it. If Soraka Q Starcall keeps missing, don’t force the poke; conserve mana.
Bard.teamfight: Heal from the very back of your team, preferably outside the enemy’s vision. Place Soraka E Equinox along Bard E Magical Journey’s entry route to stop his engage. If an ally has lost a lot of health, heal them with Soraka R Wish, but prioritize your position so Bard can’t line up Bard Q Cosmic Binding’s stun.

Sona.teamfight: Heal from the very back of your team while staying within healing range, and spread out sideways from your allies so Sona R Crescendo does not hit several of you. To prepare for Sona's late-game healing, make sure your team has at least one Grievous Wounds item and avoid extended fights.
Sona.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Sona’s main damage is magic, and Soraka has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Sona.combo: The basic sequence is to hit Sona with Soraka Q Starcall, then use Soraka W Astral Infusion to heal an ally. When Soraka Q Starcall’s slow lands, overlap it with Soraka E Equinox to make it difficult for Sona to walk out of the zone. When using Soraka Q Starcall on Sona from far away, aim in advance where she’ll retreat.
Sona.escape: The window to close the distance opens after Sona R Crescendo is down and it’s difficult for her to use the movement speed from Sona E Song of Celerity. At that point, place Soraka E Equinox where Soraka Q Starcall has slowed her to block her escape, but don’t stay forward for long.
Sona.fight: When Sona steps forward to use her aura, take a short trade with Soraka Q Starcall and get the heal. Against an opponent trying to escape with Sona E Song of Celerity, don’t rely on the slow alone; overlap Soraka E Equinox where an ally’s crowd control has landed or the opponent has been slowed. Soraka should hold her position and repeat trades instead of staying forward for a kill.
Sona.laning: Trade consistently while Sona is weak and has not built up stacks early, making her spend mana on healing. Keep up the cycle of hitting a champion with Soraka Q Starcall to restore your health, then using Soraka W Astral Infusion to heal your marksman. If Soraka Q Starcall keeps missing, reduce your poking and save mana.
Sona.phase: Pressure Sona consistently in lane early, while she has no stacks and is weak. The power Sona builds with Sona P Power Chord remains permanently, making her stronger as time goes on. In the mid and late game, use Soraka R Wish to affect fights in other lanes, but don’t let a long fight drag on against Sona in the late game.
Sona.watch: When Sona has Power Chord ready and enters basic attack range, expect bonus damage or a slow and create distance in advance. Sona R Crescendo stuns allies hit in a line, so don’t stand in a line with your allies when Sona steps forward. Sona E Song of Celerity increases her movement speed, making her difficult to chase.

Blitzcrank.build: In the early game, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads. Build magic resistance first to withstand Blitzcrank’s main damage from Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab and Blitzcrank R Static Field.
Blitzcrank.combo: After landing Soraka Q Starcall on an enemy champion, heal an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. To stop Blitzcrank’s engage or aim for a root, apply Soraka Q Starcall’s slow first, then place Soraka E Equinox over it.
Blitzcrank.escape: Right after Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab misses, look for a chance to step up and trade. If Blitzcrank approaches, place Soraka E Equinox along his engage route, then use Soraka Q Starcall’s slow and movement speed to create distance.
Blitzcrank.fight: Poke with Soraka Q Starcall right after Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab misses, and if it hits, heal an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. Save Soraka E Equinox for when Blitzcrank engages, and don’t step forward to poke.
Blitzcrank.laning: Always stand behind minions to block Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab’s path. Watch Blitzcrank’s mana, and push the lane or trade right after his grab misses. If you lose vision in brush, you can check it with Soraka Q Starcall.
Blitzcrank.phase: In the early game, stay behind minions to avoid Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab and take advantage of the window after it misses. In the mid and late game, Soraka R Wish has a shorter cooldown and can affect fights in other lanes and teamfights.
Blitzcrank.teamfight: Heal from the very back of your team, preferably outside the enemy’s vision. Place Soraka E Equinox along Blitzcrank’s approach route, and heal a badly injured ally with Soraka R Wish, which has no range limit.
Blitzcrank.watch: If Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab pulls you in, Blitzcrank E Power Fist can knock you up, followed by the silence from Blitzcrank R Static Field, so managing your distance is important. Stand behind minions, and stay far from brush when you can’t see inside it.

Brand.build: In the early game, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads. Most of Brand’s damage is magic, and Soraka has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Brand.combo: Slow Brand with Soraka Q Starcall, then layer Soraka E Equinox to aim for a root as the zone expires. While you have Rejuvenation from landing Soraka Q Starcall, healing an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion nearly removes its health cost for you and also transfers the regeneration effect.
Brand.escape: The moment Brand W Pillar of Flame is down is a chance to close the distance. Approach while watching for the stun if Brand Q Sear is also down or you aren’t ablaze, and place Soraka E Equinox along Brand’s path.
Brand.fight: When Brand W Pillar of Flame is down, poke with Soraka Q Starcall, and if it hits, heal an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. Even if you get a chance to approach Brand, don’t step forward to look for a kill, since Soraka has low health, low movement speed, and no mobility.
Brand.laning: Stand aside from burning minions to avoid Brand E Conflagration spreading. Land Soraka Q Starcall to restore your own health, then transfer the healing to your marksman with Soraka W Astral Infusion. If Soraka Q Starcall keeps missing, stop poking and conserve mana.
Brand.teamfight: Spread out from allies to avoid Brand E Conflagration spreading and Brand R Pyroclasm bouncing, and don’t stand beside an ally who is burning. Heal with Soraka W Astral Infusion from the very back of your team, and use Soraka R Wish if several allies have lost a lot of health.
Brand.watch: Dodging Brand W Pillar of Flame and Brand Q Sear first makes it easier to prevent Brand P Blaze stacks and the explosion. If you’re ablaze, move out of Brand Q Sear’s projectile path or hide behind minions to avoid its stun. Stand aside from burning minions, since Brand E Conflagration can spread from them.

Janna.build: In the early game, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first, then choose Mercury’s Treads. Janna’s damage is mostly magic, and Soraka has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Janna.combo: Hit an enemy champion with Soraka Q Starcall, then cast Soraka W Astral Infusion. When looking for a root, layer Soraka E Equinox over Soraka Q Starcall’s slow to make it hard for Janna to walk out of the zone.
Janna.escape: After Janna Q Howling Gale and Janna W Zephyr have been wasted is your chance to close the distance. If Janna is isolated from an allied damage dealer, help an engage by blocking her path with Soraka E Equinox.
Janna.fight: Pressure the ally Janna is protecting to make her use Janna E Eye Of The Storm, then deal damage once the shield is gone. Look for a chance to close the distance after Janna Q Howling Gale and Janna W Zephyr have been wasted.
Janna.laning: Hit an enemy champion with Soraka Q Starcall to restore your own health, then use that health to cast Soraka W Astral Infusion on an ally and keep the cycle going. When casting Soraka Q Starcall from far away, aim for where your opponent will step back after last-hitting. If you keep missing, stop poking and save mana.
Janna.phase: Early on, avoid the moment Janna empowers an ally with Janna E Eye Of The Storm, and keep healing by landing Soraka Q Starcall. In the mid and late game, Soraka R Wish has a shorter cooldown and can affect fights in other lanes, so use it when you can save a low-health ally. The available information does not establish which champion is stronger in the mid or late game.
Janna.teamfight: Stay at the very back of your team, preferably out of enemy vision, while keeping allies in healing range. When Janna is about to use Janna R Monsoon to knock back an engage, try to interrupt her with Soraka E Equinox. If Janna is separated from an allied damage dealer, layer Soraka E Equinox so your team can take her out first.
Janna.watch: Janna Q Howling Gale knocks you airborne. If you hear the tornado from out of sight, move out of its path. Janna E Eye Of The Storm shields its target and strengthens their counterattack, so don’t commit your damage while the shield is up. Janna R Monsoon knocks nearby enemies away, so check whether it has been used before engaging.

Karma.build: In the early game, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first to withstand Karma’s magic damage. Choose Mercury’s Treads and build magic resistance first.
Karma.combo: Hit Karma with Soraka Q Starcall first, then cast Soraka W Astral Infusion on an ally to reduce your health cost. When there’s a chance to root Karma, apply Soraka Q Starcall’s slow first, then layer Soraka E Equinox over it. Don’t expect Soraka E Equinox alone to root her.
Karma.escape: Close the distance only while Karma cannot catch you with Karma W Focused Resolve. If the shield from Karma’s E Inspire empowered by R Mantra has ended, slow her with Soraka Q Starcall and layer Soraka E Equinox to help in the fight.
Karma.fight: Dodge Karma Q Inner Flame while landing Soraka Q Starcall to restore your health, then use that health to cast Soraka W Astral Infusion on an ally. Don’t close the distance while Karma W Focused Resolve is available. Start a fight after the shield from Karma’s empowered E Inspire with R Mantra has worn off.
Karma.laning: If you can keep landing Soraka Q Starcall, manage the lane by transferring the restored health to an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. When casting Soraka Q Starcall from far away, cast it in advance at the spot where Karma will retreat after last-hitting. If it’s hard to hit, stop poking and save mana, and hold Soraka E Equinox for when Karma approaches.
Karma.phase: Early on, focus on managing distance and be especially wary of Karma’s poke and root, since Soraka has low health and movement speed. In the mid and late game, Soraka R Wish has a shorter cooldown and can affect fights in other lanes, so use it to save a heavily injured ally.
Karma.teamfight: Heal from the very back of your team, preferably out of enemy vision. If Karma W Focused Resolve is available, create distance first and bait it out; then coordinate with your allies’ engage after the shield from Karma E Inspire empowered by R Mantra has worn off. Place Soraka E Equinox in Karma’s path to block her engage with silence.
Karma.watch: Karma Q Inner Flame slows in an area and makes it easy to catch Soraka, so avoid the hit from out of range or behind minions. If you are hit by the fire zone left by Karma’s empowered Q from R Mantra, walk out of it immediately. If Karma W Focused Resolve links to you, create distance to break it before the root lands.

Leona.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle early to survive, then choose Mercury’s Treads. Magic resistance is the priority against Leona’s damage, but also consider the enemy damage dealer’s damage type when choosing what resistance to build next, since they will attack while Leona has you caught.
Leona.combo: After Leona E Zenith Blade is down, hit with Soraka Q Starcall to slow her, then layer Soraka E Equinox over it to look for a root. If hitting Soraka Q Starcall grants you Rejuvenation, heal an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. Casting Soraka W Astral Infusion repeatedly first will cost you a lot of health.
Leona.escape: The moment after Leona E Zenith Blade is down is your window to close the distance and counterattack. When Leona engages, block her path with Soraka E Equinox, and keep your distance to avoid the crowd control from Leona Q Shield of Daybreak and R Solar Flare.
Leona.fight: Bait out Leona’s engage tool, E Zenith Blade, then close the distance and counterattack. Until then, save Soraka E Equinox to stop her engage instead of using it to poke. When Leona W Eclipse is active, leave its area before it explodes.
Leona.laning: Rather than moving forward to look for kills, Soraka should poke with Soraka Q Starcall and transfer the health she restores to allies. Don’t stand in a straight line with your ranged carry, so you aren’t both exposed to Leona E Zenith Blade. If Soraka Q Starcall keeps missing, stop poking and save mana.
Leona.phase: Early on, watch out for Leona’s engage and high armor, and manage the lane with Soraka Q Starcall poke and your healing cycle. In the mid and late game, Soraka R Wish has a shorter cooldown and can affect other lanes and the map as a whole. At any stage, getting caught first makes it easy for the enemy to follow up, so prioritize your positioning.
Leona.teamfight: Heal from the very back of your team, preferably out of enemy vision. If Leona P Sunlight marks you, treat it as a signal that the enemy is about to follow up and move back immediately. Use Soraka R Wish on a heavily injured ally to increase the healing, and save Soraka E Equinox to stop Leona’s engage.
Leona.watch: Leona E Zenith Blade passes through allies and dashes to the last champion hit, so don’t stand in a straight line with your ranged carry. Leona Q Shield of Daybreak can be activated before she approaches, so dodge based on distance rather than whether she has used it. When the indicator for Leona R Solar Flare appears, move sideways to avoid the center stun.

Lulu.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, then choose Mercury’s Treads. Lulu’s damage is mostly magic, so prioritize magic resistance, but consider the damage type of the target Lulu is protecting when choosing your next resistance item.
Lulu.combo: Slow Lulu with Soraka Q Starcall, then layer Soraka E Equinox over it to make it hard for her to walk out of the zone. If Soraka Q Starcall hits a champion and grants you Rejuvenation, heal an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion afterward. Casting Soraka W Astral Infusion first costs you much more health.
Lulu.escape: After Lulu W Whimsy has been used on another ally is your chance to land Soraka Q Starcall or place Soraka E Equinox. Lulu has no dash to get herself out, so when her shield and Pix are on an allied carry, you can place Soraka E Equinox where Lulu will pass.
Lulu.fight: Repeat short trades by landing Soraka Q Starcall to restore health instead of committing heavily to one fight. Don’t move in while Lulu W Whimsy is available, and even after it has been used, move carefully and only close enough to cast Soraka E Equinox.
Lulu.laning: Stand behind minions to reduce the bonus damage from Lulu P Pix, Faerie Companion, and keep landing Soraka Q Starcall to transfer the health you restore to an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. When casting Soraka Q Starcall from far away, aim for where your opponent will step back after last-hitting. If Soraka Q Starcall keeps missing, stop poking and save mana, and hold Soraka E Equinox for a fight.
Lulu.phase: Early on, watch out for Lulu’s poke and crowd control, and survive the lane with a healing cycle built around landing Soraka Q Starcall. In the mid and late game, Soraka R Wish comes into play, so keep an eye on fights in other lanes. Even in late-game teamfights, don’t overextend to take down a target while Lulu R Wild Growth is available.
Lulu.teamfight: Heal allies with Soraka W Astral Infusion from the very back of your team, preferably out of enemy vision, and prioritize your own positioning. If Lulu R Wild Growth is available, don’t overcommit to a target it can save. Use Soraka R Wish, which has no range limit, on a heavily injured ally, and place Soraka E Equinox in the enemy’s path to stop their engage.
Lulu.watch: If Lulu W Whimsy hits you, it silences you and makes it hard to respond with healing, so keep your distance while Lulu W Whimsy is available. If Lulu Q Glitterlance slows you, it becomes easy to get caught afterward. Lulu R Wild Growth knocks up nearby enemies and can save the target you were trying to take down, so don’t approach that target.

Lux.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game. Lux deals mostly magic damage and Soraka has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first, then choose Mercury’s Treads.
Lux.combo: Hit Lux with Soraka Q Starcall first, then heal an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. If there’s a chance to root Lux, layer Soraka E Equinox where Soraka Q Starcall’s slow has landed.
Lux.escape: The moment Lux Q Light Binding misses is your chance to close the distance. Lux has no ability to create distance herself, so if you get close, slow her with Soraka Q Starcall and then layer Soraka E Equinox over it.
Lux.fight: Dodge Lux Q Light Binding, then trade from within Soraka Q Starcall range. Land Soraka Q Starcall to gain health and movement speed, and place Soraka E Equinox where the slowed Lux will pass. Don’t move deep forward to try to secure a kill as Soraka.
Lux.laning: Stand apart from your allies to the side so you aren’t hit together by Lux Q Light Binding. Hit an enemy champion with Soraka Q Starcall to restore your own health, then keep up the cycle by healing an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. If Soraka Q Starcall keeps missing, reduce your poke and save mana.
Lux.phase: Early on, getting hit by Lux Q Light Binding makes her follow-up dangerous, so Soraka should focus on surviving and manage the lane with Soraka Q Starcall and Soraka W Astral Infusion. In the mid and late game, Soraka R Wish comes into play, so keep an eye on fights in other lanes. The available information does not establish which champion is stronger in the early, mid, or late game.
Lux.teamfight: Heal from the very back of your team, preferably out of enemy vision. Don’t group with allies, so you aren’t all caught in Lux E Lucent Singularity. Use Soraka R Wish when you see a heavily injured ally, and save Soraka E Equinox in the enemy’s path.
Lux.watch: If Lux Q Light Binding hits you, you’re likely to be hit by her follow-up spells too, so bait it out and dodge before moving. Lux Q Light Binding can root up to two targets, so don’t stand in a straight line with an ally. When you see the red targeting line for Lux R Final Spark, move sideways. If you’re hit by a spell and marked by Lux P Illumination, get out of her basic attack range.

Maokai.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, then choose Mercury’s Treads. Build magic resistance first against Maokai’s damage, but also consider the enemy damage dealer’s damage while Maokai has you caught when choosing what resistance to build next.
Maokai.combo: Hit the enemy damage dealer with Soraka Q Starcall, then use Soraka W Astral Infusion to reduce your own health cost and give an ally the regeneration effect. After Maokai W Twisted Advance ends, layer Soraka E Equinox over Soraka Q Starcall’s slow to look for a root. Don’t use basic attacks or targeted abilities on Maokai while he is dashing.
Maokai.escape: The moment after Maokai W Twisted Advance is down is your window to close the distance. Enter only after dodging Maokai R Nature’s Grasp’s root as well, and place Soraka E Equinox in Maokai’s path as you engage.
Maokai.fight: Keep your distance while Maokai W Twisted Advance is ready, and save Soraka E Equinox to defend against his engage. Move forward and try to trade right after Maokai W Twisted Advance is down. If you keep hitting Maokai with spells, Maokai P Sap Magic’s heal will come back sooner, so prioritize using your poke spells on the enemy damage dealer.
Maokai.laning: Hit the enemy damage dealer with Soraka Q Starcall to restore health, then transfer it to your allied ranged carry with Soraka W Astral Infusion. If Soraka Q Starcall keeps missing, stop poking and save mana. When it’s risky to check a bush with your body, briefly reveal it with Soraka Q Starcall.
Maokai.phase: Early on, getting caught by Maokai W Twisted Advance is dangerous for Soraka, so prioritize managing your distance and building magic resistance. In the mid and late game, Soraka R Wish has a shorter cooldown and can influence other lanes and fights, so use it when you can save a low-health ally.
Maokai.teamfight: Heal from the very back of your team, preferably out of enemy vision. Fight in open terrain where there’s room to dodge Maokai R Nature’s Grasp sideways, and place Soraka E Equinox in Maokai’s engage path. Use Soraka R Wish with its increased healing on heavily injured allies in mind.
Maokai.watch: If Maokai W Twisted Advance roots you, you’re likely to be attacked afterward, so don’t close the distance near bushes while the ability is ready. Don’t enter bushes with Maokai E Sapling Toss in them, and if a sapling follows you, lure it toward a minion or monster instead of an ally. If Maokai R Nature’s Grasp approaches from far away, move perpendicular to its direction.

Milio.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, then choose Mercury’s Treads. Build magic resistance against the damage from Milio P Fired Up! and Milio Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick, but consider the enemy damage dealer’s damage type when choosing what resistance to build next. If the healing from Milio W Cozy Campfire and Milio R Breath of Life becomes a problem, get an anti-healing option earlier.
Milio.combo: Hit Milio with Soraka Q Starcall, then heal an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. When looking for a root, apply Q’s slow first, then layer Soraka E Equinox over it to make it hard for Milio to walk out of the zone.
Milio.escape: When Milio Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick is down is your chance to close the distance. Milio has no mobility spell, so once you’re close, place Soraka E Equinox to block his path.
Milio.fight: It’s better to close the distance after Milio Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick is down. Rather than moving forward to look for kills, Soraka should keep up the attrition fight by landing Soraka Q Starcall to restore health and healing an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion.
Milio.laning: Early on, aim to gain wave control by restoring health with Soraka Q Starcall poke and transferring that health to an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. When casting Q from far away, aim for where your opponent will step back after last-hitting. If Q keeps missing, stop poking and save mana.
Milio.phase: Early on, keep landing Soraka Q Starcall to aim for attrition and wave control. Milio’s composition gets stronger as time passes, so focus on depleting mana early. In the mid and late game, use Soraka R Wish to influence fights in other lanes.
Milio.teamfight: Heal from the very back of your team, preferably out of enemy vision. While Milio W Cozy Campfire is active and the enemy’s attack range is extended, delay fights on the front line. When Milio Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick is down, look for a chance for your team to target Milio himself. Use Soraka E Equinox to block engage paths, and heal a heavily injured ally with Soraka R Wish.
Milio.watch: Milio Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick can slow and displace Soraka, stopping her from approaching, so don’t force your way closer before it’s used. If the enemy ranged carry suddenly attacks from far away, Milio W Cozy Campfire is active, so delay the fight while it lasts.

Morgana.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle early to help you survive, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Morgana's main damage is magic, so build magic resistance first.
Morgana.combo: After hitting an enemy champion with Soraka Q Starcall, use Soraka W Astral Infusion to pass the regeneration effect to an ally while greatly reducing your own health cost. When looking for a root, slow them with Soraka Q Starcall first, then place Soraka E Equinox. Save Soraka E Equinox while Morgana E Black Shield is active.
Morgana.escape: Morgana has no skill that creates distance on her own, so look to close in when Morgana Q Dark Binding misses and Morgana E Black Shield is down. Soraka has no skill to escape on her own, so don't stay in Morgana R Soul Shackles range for long.
Morgana.fight: Keep enough distance and an angle to dodge Morgana Q Dark Binding, and poke with Soraka Q Starcall. Don't waste Soraka E Equinox on a target protected by Morgana E Black Shield. Close the distance after Black Shield and Dark Binding are down, then overlap Soraka E Equinox with the slow from Soraka Q Starcall.
Morgana.laning: Keep minions between you and Morgana to block Morgana Q Dark Binding. Hit an enemy champion with Soraka Q Starcall to restore your health, then heal an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. If Soraka Q Starcall keeps missing, reduce your poke and save mana.
Morgana.phase: Early on, if Soraka gets hit by Morgana Q Dark Binding once, it's easy to take follow-up attacks, so prioritize spacing and magic resistance. In the mid game, keep up the pattern of hitting with Soraka Q Starcall and healing an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. As the mid-to-late game progresses, Soraka R Wish has a shorter cooldown and can affect fights in other lanes.
Morgana.teamfight: Heal from the very back of your team, ideally outside the enemy’s vision. Save Soraka E Equinox for the path Morgana takes when engaging, and if Morgana R Soul Shackles catches you, move out of range before the stun. Heal an ally with Soraka R Wish when you see that their health has dropped substantially.
Morgana.watch: If Morgana Q Dark Binding hits you, Morgana W Tormented Shadow and follow-up attacks will follow, so keep minions between you and Morgana as you move. Morgana W Tormented Shadow hurts more at lower health, so avoid stepping into its area when retreating. If Morgana R Soul Shackles catches you, get out of range before the stun triggers.

Nami.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, then choose Mercury’s Treads. Nami’s damage is mostly magic, and Soraka has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Nami.combo: Hit Nami with Soraka Q Starcall, then cast Soraka W Astral Infusion. While Soraka Q Starcall’s slow is active, layer Soraka E Equinox to make it hard for her to leave the zone and set up a root.
Nami.escape: Engage right after Nami Q Aqua Prison misses. Once Nami E Tidecaller’s Blessing has worn off and you’ve also dodged Nami R Tidal Wave, look for a chance to close in on Nami, who has no mobility ability, and place Soraka E Equinox.
Nami.fight: The moment Nami Q Aqua Prison misses is your chance to target Nami. She has low health and no mobility spell, so before forcing your way closer, slow her with Soraka Q Starcall and layer Soraka E Equinox over it.
Nami.laning: Aim for a cycle of hitting Nami with Soraka Q Starcall to restore your own health, then healing an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. If Soraka Q Starcall keeps missing, stop poking and save mana, and hold Soraka E Equinox to stop Nami from approaching.
Nami.phase: Early on, getting caught by Nami’s crowd control makes it easy to get hit repeatedly, so prioritize managing distance and building magic resistance. In the mid and late game, Soraka R Wish has a shorter cooldown and can influence other lanes and fights.
Nami.teamfight: Stay at the very back of your team and out of enemy vision, and cast Soraka W Astral Infusion on allies within range. If Nami R Tidal Wave appears, dodge sideways. Use Soraka R Wish when you can save a heavily injured ally.
Nami.watch: Nami Q Aqua Prison stuns, and Nami R Tidal Wave knocks you airborne and sets up follow-up attacks. When you see either one coming, walk sideways to dodge. Keep your distance from an enemy affected by Nami E Tidecaller’s Blessing until the effect ends.

Nautilus.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Nautilus’s main damage is magic, so build magic resistance first.
Nautilus.combo: Hit Nautilus with Soraka Q Starcall, then heal an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. When looking for a root, overlap Soraka E Equinox where Soraka Q Starcall has slowed him.
Nautilus.escape: If Nautilus Q Dredge Line misses, close in only while that engage tool is down to look for Soraka Q Starcall. Then use Soraka E Equinox to block the path Nautilus would take and retreat again.
Nautilus.fight: Trade right after Nautilus Q Dredge Line misses. Slow him with Soraka Q Starcall, overlap Soraka E Equinox, then create distance before Nautilus can reach you with a basic attack.
Nautilus.laning: Stand with minions between you and Nautilus to stop Nautilus Q Dredge Line's engage. Hit with Soraka Q Starcall to restore health, then pass that health to an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion; if Q keeps missing, stop poking and save mana. Save Soraka E Equinox for when Nautilus engages.
Nautilus.phase: Early on, keep your distance and survive without getting hit by follow-up crowd control after Nautilus Q Dredge Line catches you. In the mid-to-late game, Soraka R Wish can affect fights in other lanes, so watch for allies who have lost a large amount of health. The provided information isn't enough to determine which champion is stronger at each stage.
Nautilus.teamfight: Heal from the very back of your team, ideally outside the enemy's vision. If Nautilus R Depth Charge is available, don't stand in line with an ally or an engage path, and place Soraka E Equinox where Nautilus will enter.
Nautilus.watch: Nautilus Q Dredge Line starts his engage, so dodge it with minions between you. After it catches you, Nautilus P Staggering Blow's root and Nautilus R Depth Charge's crowd control can follow, so don't stay in basic attack range either.

Pantheon.build: Pantheon Q Comet Spear, W Shield Vault, and E Aegis Assault deal primarily physical damage, so buy armor items first. Pantheon W Shield Vault deals damage based on your maximum health, so avoid choices that only add a large amount of health.
Pantheon.combo: Hit Pantheon with Soraka Q Starcall to slow him and gain Rejuvenation, then heal an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. When looking for a root, overlap Soraka E Equinox where Soraka Q Starcall has slowed him.
Pantheon.escape: Look to engage while Pantheon W Shield Vault is down and can't immediately stun you, and before Pantheon R Grand Starfall comes back up. Place Soraka E Equinox along Pantheon's path to block his engage or retreat.
Pantheon.fight: Don't trade blows with Pantheon early; poke with Soraka Q Starcall from outside Pantheon W Shield Vault range. If Pantheon E Aegis Assault is active, don't attack from the front; wait until it ends.
Pantheon.laning: Stand with minions between you and Pantheon to block Pantheon Q Comet Spear's poke. Save Soraka E Equinox for the path Pantheon will take when engaging, instead of using it to poke. If Soraka Q Starcall keeps missing, stop poking and save mana.
Pantheon.phase: Pantheon's influence falls off as the game moves toward the late game, so Soraka should survive, keep healing, and use Soraka R Wish to join fights in other lanes.
Pantheon.teamfight: Heal from the very back of your team, ideally outside the enemy's vision, and don't let Pantheon get within Pantheon W Shield Vault range. Place Soraka E Equinox along Pantheon's engage path, and use Soraka R Wish on an ally who has lost a large amount of health.
Pantheon.watch: Pantheon W Shield Vault targets and stuns, so create distance before you enter its range. When you see the landing warning for Pantheon R Grand Starfall, walk out of the landing area.

Pyke.build: Get health first to prepare for Pyke's damage, and if you build resistance, choose armor. Pyke stacks physical penetration, so get enough health to stay above the execute threshold instead of building only a small amount of armor.
Pyke.combo: Hit Pyke with Soraka Q Starcall first to slow him and gain Rejuvenation, then heal an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. When there's a chance to root Pyke, overlap Soraka E Equinox where Soraka Q Starcall has slowed him. It's hard to expect a root if you place Soraka E Equinox first by itself.
Pyke.escape: Even if Pyke E Phantom Undertow is down, don't rush to engage while Pyke R Death From Below is still available. When both movement abilities are down, slow Pyke with Soraka Q Starcall and overlap Soraka E Equinox to block his escape route.
Pyke.fight: Soraka should keep her distance first and use Soraka Q Starcall to gain a slow and heal. When Pyke engages, place Soraka E Equinox along his path to silence him, and sidestep Pyke E Phantom Undertow's stun path. Don't use Soraka E Equinox to poke and give Pyke an opening to engage.
Pyke.laning: Hit Pyke with Soraka Q Starcall to restore your health, then use Soraka W Astral Infusion to pass that health to an ally as you manage the lane. If Soraka Q Starcall keeps missing, stop poking and save mana. When it's risky to check a bush yourself, briefly reveal it with Soraka Q Starcall.
Pyke.phase: Early on, prioritize watching for Pyke's engage, managing Soraka's distance, and saving Soraka E Equinox. In the mid-to-late game, use Soraka R Wish to save allies who have lost a large amount of health, as it can affect fights in other lanes. In the late game, move with your team and keep low-health allies Pyke may target behind the frontline.
Pyke.teamfight: Heal from the very back of your team, ideally outside the enemy's vision. Keep your distance from wounded allies so Pyke R Death From Below doesn't chain onto low-health allies. When Pyke engages, place Soraka E Equinox along his path, and use Soraka R Wish to heal an ally who has lost a large amount of health.
Pyke.watch: If Pyke Q Bone Skewer pulls you or Pyke E Phantom Undertow stuns you, Soraka's lack of mobility makes it difficult to avoid the follow-up attacks. When Pyke E Phantom Undertow starts, move to the side of its dash path, and if you see a shark shadow beneath your feet, retreat toward an ally or turret. Don't stand near an ally with low enough health to be hit by Pyke R Death From Below.

Rakan.build: In the early game, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Rakan's damage is mainly magic, so build magic resistance before armor, then prioritize considering a way to remove crowd control.
Rakan.combo: Hit Rakan with Soraka Q Starcall first to slow him and gain Rejuvenation, then overlap Soraka E Equinox to look for a root. After that, use Soraka W Astral Infusion on an ally to greatly reduce your health cost and pass on the regeneration effect.
Rakan.escape: The moment after Rakan W Grand Entrance is down is a chance to close in. Rakan E Battle Dance can only be used on allied champions, so chain Soraka Q Starcall and Soraka E Equinox against Rakan when he is separated from his allies.
Rakan.fight: Look to trade right after Rakan P Fey Feathers' shield is removed. After Rakan W Grand Entrance misses, close in, slow him with Soraka Q Starcall, and overlap Soraka E Equinox.
Rakan.laning: If Rakan W Grand Entrance catches you once, follow-up hits are easy, so keep your distance and don't use Soraka E Equinox to poke. Hit an enemy champion with Soraka Q Starcall to restore your health, then use Soraka W Astral Infusion on an ally as you manage the lane. If Soraka Q Starcall keeps missing, reduce your poke and save mana.
Rakan.phase: Early on, Rakan's engage starting with Rakan W Grand Entrance is threatening, so Soraka should focus on managing distance. In the mid-to-late game, the shorter cooldown on Soraka R Wish makes her more able to help with fights in other lanes. In late-game team fights, Soraka should still survive at the back and keep healing.
Rakan.teamfight: Stand at the very back of your team, ideally outside the enemy's vision. Place Soraka E Equinox at Rakan W Grand Entrance's landing point or along the path he will take, and don't line up with your allies so Rakan R The Quickness doesn't catch several of you together. If an ally has lost a large amount of health, use Soraka R Wish to heal them from across the battlefield.
Rakan.watch: Rakan W Grand Entrance knocks up at the visible landing point after the dash, so sidestep when Rakan starts moving. Rakan R The Quickness is difficult to dodge on foot once active, so don't line up with your allies, and place Soraka E Equinox along the engage path before he reaches you.

Rell.build: In the early game, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Rell's damage is mainly magic, and Soraka tends to have low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Rell.combo: Slow Rell with Soraka Q Starcall, then overlap Soraka E Equinox to look for a root. After gaining Rejuvenation from a hit with Soraka Q Starcall, heal an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion to reduce your health cost.
Rell.escape: Create distance right after Rell uses Rell W Ferromancy: Crash Down, and look to engage after Rell E Full Tilt is also down. Then slow her with Soraka Q Starcall and overlap Soraka E Equinox to make it harder for Rell to escape.
Rell.fight: Poke with Soraka Q Starcall from outside Rell W Ferromancy: Crash Down range, and if it hits, pass the healing you gain to an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. When Rell charges in, block her path with Soraka E Equinox and create distance.
Rell.laning: Rell has low magic resistance early and can't restore her health in lane, so keep landing Soraka Q Starcall from outside her engage range to wear her down. Save Soraka E Equinox for Rell's engage instead of using it to poke. If Soraka Q Starcall keeps missing, stop poking and save mana.
Rell.phase: Early on, it's a good approach to avoid Rell's engage while wearing down Rell, who has no way to restore her health, with Soraka Q Starcall. In the mid-to-late game, Soraka R Wish has a shorter cooldown and can affect fights in other lanes and across the map. At any stage, if Rell catches Soraka, follow-up attacks are easy, so prioritize keeping your distance.
Rell.teamfight: Heal from the very back of your team, ideally outside the enemy's vision, and space out from allies so Rell R Magnet Storm doesn't catch several of you. Place Soraka E Equinox along Rell's engage path, and use Soraka R Wish to heal an ally when you see that they have lost a large amount of health.
Rell.watch: When Rell E Full Tilt speeds up Rell and her ally together, treat it as an engage signal, stop trading, and retreat outside Rell W Ferromancy: Crash Down range. Rell Q Shattering Strike comes in a straight line, so dodge sideways, and space out from allies so Rell R Magnet Storm doesn't pull several of you together.

Renata.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Renata Glasc deals mostly magic damage, and Soraka has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Renata.combo: After hitting Renata Glasc with Soraka Q Starcall, use Soraka W Astral Infusion to heal an ally. When you have a chance to catch Renata Glasc, apply Soraka Q Starcall’s slow first, then overlap it with Soraka E Equinox so she has difficulty leaving the zone.
Renata.escape: The window to close the distance opens after Renata Glasc Q Handshake is down. Renata Glasc has no built-in mobility, so if an ally approaches, slow her with Soraka Q Starcall, then place Soraka E Equinox on her escape route. If Renata Glasc R Hostile Takeover is still available, don’t go in grouped with your allies.
Renata.fight: When Renata Glasc Q Handshake is down, poke with Soraka Q Starcall, then use Soraka W Astral Infusion to transfer the health you recover on hit to an ally. Renata Glasc has no built-in mobility, but neither does Soraka, so instead of going deep yourself, use Soraka E Equinox to block a choke point when an ally has closed the distance.
Renata.laning: Renata Glasc has relatively low health and attack damage early, so pressure her from a position where you can hit Soraka Q Starcall. From far away, place Soraka Q Starcall where she’ll retreat after last-hitting, and if you keep missing, stop poking to save mana. Save Soraka E Equinox to block the engage that can follow after Renata Glasc Q Handshake catches you.
Renata.phase: Pressure Renata Glasc with Soraka Q Starcall early while her health and attack damage are low, but don’t repeatedly cast Soraka W Astral Infusion without Starcall’s blessing and drain your own health. In the mid and late game, use Soraka R Wish to affect fights in other lanes and teamfights, and keep your distance from allies in fights where Renata Glasc R Hostile Takeover is available. The available information isn’t enough to determine who has the overall advantage in the mid and late game.
Renata.teamfight: Stay at the very back of your team, preferably out of the enemy’s vision, while keeping within healing range. Keep your distance from allies so Renata Glasc R Hostile Takeover doesn’t hit several of you at once, and place Soraka E Equinox in the choke points enemies have to pass through. If an ally loses a large amount of health, heal your whole team with Soraka R Wish.
Renata.watch: Renata Glasc Q Handshake roots its target and can throw them into an ally to stun them too, so stand behind minions or your frontline. While Renata Glasc R Hostile Takeover is available, keep your distance from allies and don’t engage bunched up in a line. If you kill an enemy affected by Renata Glasc W Bailout, don’t overextend to chase them after they revive; fall back with your allies.

Senna.build: Senna’s main damage is physical, so build armor first. Senna P Absolution adds damage based on the target’s current health to her basic attacks, so build armor alongside health instead of stacking only health.
Senna.combo: Hit Senna with Soraka Q Starcall to slow her, then overlap Soraka E Equinox where she’ll pass. When you have Starcall’s blessing from landing Q, use Soraka W Astral Infusion to heal an ally and reduce your own health cost. Avoid starting with W.
Senna.escape: The window to close the distance opens after Senna W Last Embrace misses or is down. Senna has no ability to create distance on her own, so after approaching, combine Soraka E Equinox with Soraka Q Starcall’s slow to block her escape route.
Senna.fight: Trade by hitting Soraka Q Starcall to restore your health, then using Soraka W Astral Infusion to heal an ally. Look for Senna to step forward to collect a soul, but if your Q keeps missing, stop poking and save mana.
Senna.laning: Watch the soul locations and poke with Soraka Q Starcall when Senna steps forward to collect one, disrupting her collection. From far away, place Q where Senna will retreat after last-hitting. Move out of the straight line of Senna Q Piercing Darkness, and stand behind minions when watching for Senna W Last Embrace.
Senna.phase: Senna has low health and attack damage early, so you have a chance to poke her when she steps forward to collect a soul. In the mid and late game, Soraka R Wish can affect fights in other lanes too. If you leave Senna alone early, her range and attack damage will keep growing, so keep disrupting her soul collection.
Senna.teamfight: Heal from the very back of your team, preferably out of the enemy’s vision. When Senna E Curse of the Black Mist appears, fall back to a spot with vision and place Soraka E Equinox on the approach path. Use Soraka R Wish on a badly injured ally to increase the healing they receive.
Senna.watch: Senna Q Piercing Darkness travels in a straight line through Senna and an ally or minion, so move out of that line. Dodge Senna W Last Embrace from behind minions, and if it hits you, move away from allies while the mark is visible so they aren’t rooted with you. After getting hit once, fall back to prevent her from landing a second attack and collecting mist.

Seraphine.build: In the early game, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Seraphine's main damage is magic, and Soraka tends to have low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Seraphine.combo: Hit Seraphine with Soraka Q Starcall first to slow her and gain Rejuvenation. Overlap Soraka E Equinox on the slowed Seraphine to look for a root when the area ends, then heal an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. Using W before Q costs Soraka much more health.
Seraphine.escape: The moment after dodging Seraphine E Beat Drop is a window to pressure her. If Seraphine is separated from an allied marksman, slow her with Soraka Q Starcall and overlap Soraka E Equinox. Soraka has no skill to escape on her own, so don't force a close approach while Seraphine E Beat Drop is available.
Seraphine.fight: Trade by hitting with Soraka Q Starcall to restore your health instead of moving too far forward. The chance to pressure Seraphine comes when Seraphine E Beat Drop is down and Seraphine is separated from allies. At that point, follow the slow from Soraka Q Starcall with Soraka E Equinox.
Seraphine.laning: Aim for a cycle of hitting an enemy champion with Soraka Q Starcall, then healing an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. If Q keeps missing, stop poking and save mana. Keep your distance while Seraphine E Beat Drop is available, and save Soraka E Equinox for a fight.
Seraphine.teamfight: Heal from the very back of your team, ideally outside the enemy's vision. Spread out to the sides from your allies so Seraphine R Encore can't gain range by following them. Help an ally who has lost a large amount of health with Soraka W Astral Infusion, and heal with Soraka R Wish if several allies are in danger.
Seraphine.watch: Seraphine E Beat Drop roots slowed targets, so if you're slowed, move out of the straight line in front of Seraphine. Seraphine R Encore gains range each time it hits a champion, so don't line up with your allies. When your health is low, also watch out for Seraphine Q High Note, which deals damage based on missing health.

Taric.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game to withstand Taric’s magic damage. Choose Mercury's Treads for boots and prioritize magic resistance.
Taric.combo: Hit Taric with Soraka Q Starcall, then use Soraka W Astral Infusion to heal an ally. When looking to root him, land Soraka Q Starcall’s slow first, then overlap Soraka E Equinox on top of it. Place Soraka E Equinox in Taric’s approach path too, to block his engage.
Taric.escape: The moment after Taric E Dazzle is down is your chance to close the distance and poke. Taric has no ability to create distance on his own, so if there’s an opening for you and your allies to catch him, place Soraka E Equinox on his escape route. Soraka has no mobility, so don’t approach first before you have dodged the stun.
Taric.fight: After dodging Taric E Dazzle, keep your range and poke with Soraka Q Starcall. Don’t fight close for long, so you don’t get hit by Taric P Bravado’s empowered basic attacks. While Taric R Cosmic Radiance’s damage immunity is active, restrict his movement with Soraka E Equinox, then attack after the immunity ends.
Taric.laning: Build a cycle of hitting an enemy champion with Soraka Q Starcall to restore your health, then transferring that health to an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. If Soraka Q Starcall keeps missing, reduce your poking to save mana. Don’t use Soraka E Equinox for poke; save it to block an engage led by Taric E Dazzle.
Taric.phase: Taric’s melee basic attacks are strong early, so Soraka should keep her distance and poke after Taric E Dazzle is down. In the mid and late game, Soraka R Wish’s cooldown gets shorter, letting her affect fights in other lanes and teamfights. The available information isn’t enough to determine who is stronger in the mid or late game.
Taric.teamfight: Heal from the very back of your team, preferably out of the enemy’s vision. If you see Taric R Cosmic Radiance’s cast animation, pull your allies back, and restrict the enemy’s movement with Soraka E Equinox while damage immunity is active. Resume attacking when it ends, and use Soraka R Wish to heal any badly injured allies.
Taric.watch: When you see the tell for Taric E Dazzle, move sideways to dodge it. Stop attacking while Taric R Cosmic Radiance’s damage immunity is active, then attack again as soon as it ends.

Thresh.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Build magic resistance against Thresh’s main ability damage, but prioritize tenacity when getting caught would also leave you exposed to allied damage.
Thresh.combo: When Thresh engages, slow him with Soraka Q Starcall, then overlap Soraka E Equinox on his path. If Soraka Q Starcall hits an enemy champion, use Soraka W Astral Infusion to heal an ally while you have Starcall’s blessing.
Thresh.escape: Only close the distance to poke after Thresh Q Death Sentence misses and Thresh W Dark Passage is down too. If Thresh E Flay is still available, don’t stand where he can pull you, and place Soraka E Equinox in the path Thresh has to take.
Thresh.fight: Poke with Soraka Q Starcall when Thresh walks forward to collect souls or when Thresh Q Death Sentence misses. Soraka has no ability to escape, so keep your distance and continue healing instead of going deep for a kill.
Thresh.laning: Move side to side to account for Thresh Q Death Sentence, and change direction once more when stepping forward. Hit an enemy champion with Soraka Q Starcall to restore your health, then use Soraka W Astral Infusion to heal an ally. Don’t use Soraka E Equinox for poke; save it to block Thresh’s approach path.
Thresh.phase: Early on, once Soraka is caught, it’s easy to get hit by follow-up attacks, so avoid Thresh’s engage and manage your distance. As time passes, Thresh becomes tanky with the souls he collects, while Soraka can affect fights in other lanes in the mid and late game with Soraka R Wish. The available information isn’t enough to determine who is stronger in the mid or late game.
Thresh.teamfight: Stand at the very back of your team, preferably out of the enemy’s vision, and heal from there. Place Soraka E Equinox in Thresh’s approach path, and use Soraka R Wish when an ally loses a large amount of health. If you’re trapped in Thresh R The Box, immediately choose which direction to break through and have your toughest ally pass through one wall first.
Thresh.watch: If Thresh Q Death Sentence hits you, his dash and the forced movement from Thresh E Flay can put you in danger next. Move sideways when you see him raise his hook, and don’t stand on the line between Thresh and his ally.

Velkoz.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Build magic resistance first against Vel'Koz’s main ability damage, but focus on avoiding consecutive hits, since resistance can’t block the true damage from Vel'Koz P Organic Deconstruction or Vel'Koz R Life Form Disintegration Ray.
Velkoz.combo: Hit Vel'Koz with Soraka Q Starcall, then use Soraka W Astral Infusion to heal an ally. When looking to root him, apply Soraka Q Starcall’s slow first, then overlap it with Soraka E Equinox to make it difficult for Vel'Koz to leave the zone.
Velkoz.escape: The window to close the distance opens after Vel'Koz E Tectonic Disruption is down. Vel'Koz has no mobility, so if an ally approaches, overlap Soraka E Equinox, but don’t step forward first and get hit by Vel'Koz’s chain of abilities.
Velkoz.fight: Use the time after Vel'Koz E Tectonic Disruption is down to trade. Hit with Soraka Q Starcall to gain a slow and restore your health, and overlap Soraka E Equinox when an ally who has closed the distance catches Vel'Koz. If Vel'Koz R Life Form Disintegration Ray starts, interrupt it immediately with Soraka E Equinox.
Velkoz.laning: Aim for a cycle of landing Soraka Q Starcall to restore your health, then transferring that health to an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. When using Q from far away, place it where you expect Vel'Koz to retreat, and if you keep missing, stop poking to save mana. Be careful: repeatedly using Soraka W Astral Infusion without healing yourself will drain your own health first.
Velkoz.teamfight: Stay at the very back of your team, within healing range, and prioritize keeping yourself safe. If Vel'Koz R Life Form Disintegration Ray starts, prioritize interrupting it with Soraka E Equinox. If you see a badly injured ally, heal them with Soraka R Wish, which has no range limit.
Velkoz.watch: Vel'Koz Q Plasma Fission can hit you with the split beams too, so don’t just dodge sideways; move behind the beam after it passes. If you’re knocked up by Vel'Koz E Tectonic Disruption and hit by a series of abilities, Vel'Koz P Organic Deconstruction’s true damage will trigger, so retreat and let it expire when stacks are applied.

Xerath.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Xerath deals mostly magic damage, and Soraka has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Xerath.combo: Hit Xerath with Soraka Q Starcall, then use Soraka W Astral Infusion to heal an ally. When you have a chance to root Xerath, land Soraka Q Starcall’s slow first and overlap Soraka E Equinox so he has difficulty leaving the zone.
Xerath.escape: Xerath has no mobility, so close the distance during the window when Xerath E Shocking Orb and Xerath W Eye of Destruction are down. You can also approach while dodging to the side when Xerath is slowed as he charges Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Once you’re close, use Soraka E Equinox to block Xerath’s escape route.
Xerath.fight: The window to close the distance opens just after Xerath E Shocking Orb and Xerath W Eye of Destruction are down. Still, Soraka should trade by restoring her health with Soraka Q Starcall and healing an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion, rather than stepping forward to try for a kill.
Xerath.laning: If you survive Xerath’s long-range poke without taking heavy damage, there will be a point when mana runs out first. Push the lane then and call your jungler. If Soraka Q Starcall keeps missing, stop poking and save mana.
Xerath.phase: Early on, withstand Xerath’s range with a Null-Magic Mantle. If Xerath runs out of mana during lane, push the lane and create an opportunity with your jungler. In the mid and late game, Soraka R Wish’s cooldown gets shorter, allowing you to affect fights in other lanes too.
Xerath.teamfight: Stand at the very back of your team, preferably out of the enemy’s vision. Dodge Xerath E Shocking Orb’s stun, and after Soraka Q Starcall hits, use Soraka W Astral Infusion to heal an ally. If you see an ally who has lost a large amount of health, heal them with Soraka R Wish.
Xerath.watch: If you’re stunned by Xerath E Shocking Orb, you can get hit by follow-up attacks too, so prioritize dodging that shot. Xerath Q Arcanopulse passes through minions, so when you see him charging it, change direction and move to the side. Start dodging immediately when you see the cast animation for Xerath R Rite of the Arcane.

Zilean.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Zilean deals magic damage, so Soraka should build magic resistance first. Tenacity is also important when you're held back by bomb stuns and by slows.
Zilean.combo: Hit Zilean with Soraka Q Starcall, then heal an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. When there's a chance to catch Zilean, land Q's slow first and overlap Soraka E Equinox to make it difficult for him to leave the area.
Zilean.escape: If you've closed in, slow them with Soraka Q Starcall and overlap Soraka E Equinox.
Zilean.laning: Keep up the cycle of hitting an enemy champion with Soraka Q Starcall to restore your health, then healing an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. When throwing Q from far away, place it in advance where Zilean will stand after last-hitting and backing off. If Q keeps missing, stop poking and conserve mana.
Zilean.phase: In the mid to late game, use Soraka R Wish to influence fights in other lanes.
Zilean.teamfight: Soraka heals from the very back of her team's formation, preferably outside the enemy's vision. Use Soraka R Wish on an ally who has lost a lot of health, and don't waste abilities while a target protected by Zilean R Chronoshift is reviving. If it's difficult to finish off an allied damage dealer, it's better to switch your target to squishy Zilean himself.
Zilean.watch: Zilean Q Time Bomb stuns when two bombs attach to the same target. When the first bomb attaches, move away from your allies and get outside the blast radius. Be especially wary of another bomb following when Zilean E Time Warp slows you. Don't use abilities on a target affected by Zilean R Chronoshift while they are reviving.

Zyra.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Zyra deals mostly magic damage, and Soraka has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Zyra.combo: After Zyra E Grasping Roots is down, slow her with Soraka Q Starcall, then overlap Soraka E Equinox to make it difficult for her to leave the area. If Soraka Q Starcall hits a champion, heal an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion to reduce your own health cost.
Zyra.escape: Your chance to close the distance comes after dodging Zyra E Grasping Roots, when there are no plants nearby. Zyra has no mobility spell, but Soraka has no skill to escape on her own either, so don't engage while Zyra E Grasping Roots is still available.
Zyra.fight: Dodge Zyra E Grasping Roots sideways, then poke with Soraka Q Starcall from an area without plants. Zyra has no mobility spell, giving you a chance to close the distance, but Soraka has no escape skill either, so don't move forward before dodging the root.
Zyra.laning: Use Soraka Q Starcall to check vision in bushes where Zyra has spent a long time, and don't walk in to step on seeds while abilities are flying toward you. Keep up the cycle of hitting an enemy champion with Soraka Q Starcall to restore your health, then healing an ally with Soraka W Astral Infusion. If Soraka Q Starcall keeps missing, reduce your poke and conserve mana.
Zyra.phase: The available information isn't enough to determine who is stronger in the early, middle, or late game. In the early game, hold on with magic resistance and careful spacing while landing Soraka Q Starcall to keep healing. In the mid to late game, use Soraka R Wish to influence fights in other lanes, and move fights away from areas where Zyra has stockpiled seeds.
Zyra.teamfight: Heal from the very back of your team's formation, preferably outside the enemy's vision, and prioritize keeping yourself safe. Don't take fights where Zyra has stockpiled plants; move to another spot. When you see the cast indicator for Zyra R Stranglethorns, walk out of its area, and use Soraka R Wish on an ally who has lost a lot of health.
Zyra.watch: If Zyra E Grasping Roots hits you with its straight-line root, Zyra R Stranglethorns and plant damage can follow, so dodge sideways at the edge of its range. When you see the cast indicator for Zyra R Stranglethorns, walk out of its area before the knock-up. If there are lots of plants in an area, briefly back off and wait for them to disappear.
